Vacate orders were in place on Thursday at buildings adjacent to site of the collapsed Brooklyn apartment building. Residents of other buildings who were temporarily displaced were allowed to return home, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
Gov. Kathy Hochul of New York called the collapse “absolutely, absolutely” heartbreaking on Thursday morning at a news media event on a small business initiative in Harlem. She said her office remained in contact with the city and that the state was ready to provide resources if needed. Ms. Hochul also sang praises of the Fire Department and its quick response.
“New Yorkers are stunned by what they’re seeing, but the investigators are already at work,” she said. “And New Yorkers deserve to know how and why this happened, and they’ll get to the bottom of it.”
Nearly 24 hours after a three-story apartment building collapsed in Brooklyn, rescue workers remain locked in a fight to identify and rescue any survivors trapped in the rubble.
The extensive search and rescue operations have involved canine units, helicopters and excavation machinery. So far, eight people have been confirmed dead and over a dozen are injured. Fire officials have said the search efforts are likely to continue for days.
It is not yet clear why the building, in the Flatbush neighborhood, collapsed. But the Fire Department’s search and rescue mission is following a standard playbook, one that dates back to World War II. It has been deployed countless times after similar disasters around the world, including the 2010 earthquake in Haiti and a condo collapse in 2021 in Surfside, Fla., that killed nearly 100 people.
Here’s how these search and rescue operations work.
What happens first?
After determining the basics of the collapsed building — including whether it is residential or commercial — rescuers look for any people who may be trapped on the surface of the wreckage, said Dave Downey, a retired fire chief from Miami-Dade County in Florida who has responded to many disasters involving collapsed buildings, including the Sept. 11 terror attacks and the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.
After that, Mr. Downey said, rescuers try to determine the manner in which the building collapsed, which informs their further search efforts.
If the building is still partially standing and there is open space between the floors, there could be more survivable space for any people trapped inside. Rescuers would then start looking inside these so-called void spaces, “the areas where there’s the greatest chance for survival,” Mr. Downey said.
Search efforts are of course more difficult when a building falls apart in a way that leaves little open space, as happened with the Surfside condo, which collapsed like a pancake, floor by floor, according to Mr. Downey.
What other factors must rescuers account for?
Rescuers need to also consider external factors like the weather. In the case of the Flatbush collapse, rainy conditions on Thursday afternoon may complicate the rescue efforts.
“You want to control any of the utilities, whether it’s gas, whether it’s water, whether it’s power,” Mr. Downey said. “You certainly don’t want water flooding any of these void spaces.”
Water mains were shut off temporarily after the collapse, but by noon on Thursday water service in the area had been restored, according to the city’s Department of Environmental Protection.
Rescuers may also seek to stabilize whatever parts of the building remain standing. That could mean using wood to shore up parts of the structure, allowing workers to access the rubble where more survivors could be trapped.
What technology is used?
When looking for survivors, rescuers tend to use specialized equipment like drones, listening devices and search cameras.
In Brooklyn, the Police Department has deployed drones to capture the scene while members of its aviation unit search from the sky, a police spokeswoman said on Thursday. Officers from the department’s Emergency Service Unit were also searching the area with dogs from the K-9 team.
Heavy equipment like grapplers were also being used on Thursday to remove rubble, said Lillian Bonsignore, the fire commissioner.
When does an operation turn to recovery?
Ms. Bonsignore said on Thursday afternoon that the operation was still focused on rescuing survivors. But at a certain point, officials will have to make the difficult choice to shift the operation to recovery, Mr. Downey said.
“When the decision is made that we no longer have persons that have survived, we transition to recovery,” Mr. Downey said.
Such a determination can take days and depends on a complex set of factors. One of the last to be considered is the amount of time that has elapsed since the collapse, Mr. Downey said. More important is the safety of the rescuers, which has to be weighed against the chances that anyone is still alive.
Still, a transition to recovery does not preclude the possibility that survivors will be found. When he was in Haiti after the 2010 earthquake, Mr. Downey said, his team found a 2-year-old child alive in the rubble of a building eight days after it collapsed.
“We promise, with everything we have, we will not stop working until everyone is rescued or recovered,” Ms. Bonsignore said.
Chelsia Rose Marcius, Caitlyn Freeman and Hurubie Meko contributed reporting.
The consul general of Ecuador, Gicela Andrade, has been visiting with city officials at a staging area near the scene. Andrade said that at least two Ecuadorians have been identified as victims. The remains of one, Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, will be sent to Ecuador to be buried, she said. Andrade accompanied Leanor Yupa, the mother of a second Ecuadorian victim, Gabriel Ariolfo Siguencia, to meet with detectives this afternoon.“When we heard the sad news we immediately got to ground zero where this tragedy occured and we’ve been in contact with the mother of one of these victims who has been missing since yesterday,” Andrade said in Spanish. “The authorities have just confirmed the death of our compatriot, and his mother was in that moment learning of the death of her son.”
Monzurat Oni, the chairwoman of Brooklyn’s Community Board 17, where the collapse took place, said the developer of the construction site did not come to a board meeting this year to answer the public’s questions about the project. Under ballot measures passed last year that sped up the process for housing projects, the community board has less input, she said, even as the neighborhood is seeing a surge in new developments.
“I’m not against new construction,” Oni said. “I know New York needs to grow. We want new construction to be responsive to the existing community.”
Julie Menin, the City Council speaker, began her comments at a council meeting on Thursday with a moment of silence for the victims of the building collapse.
“Today, my colleagues and I joined New Yorkers across the five boroughs in mourning the eight lives that were lost in the tragic collapse of a building in Flatbush,” she said, adding, “We’re incredibly grateful for the approximately 250 first responders who raced to the scene and who have been working tirelessly throughout the night on this heroic rescue efforts.”
She added that she was praying for the recovery of those injured.
As uniformed firefighters entered closed storefronts beside the collapsed building, representatives from the mayor’s office visited nearby businesses that remained open. With the streets blocked with emergency vehicles, the city’s representatives offered to help with any problems getting packages delivered or trash removed.
First responders, investigators and city officials have a hard job in the wake of a building collapse: finding missing people, securing the area and notifying family members. A Y.M.C.A. on Flatbush Avenue has become a de facto staging area for families looking for information regarding loved ones. Throughout Thursday, teary people have entered the recreation center searching for information. A representative from Ecuador’s government visited the site earlier, accompanying the family of Gabriel Siguencia as they sought to confirm their son’s death. Aid groups and local restuarants, including the nearby Chick-fil-A, are dropping off supplies.
A spokesperson for the American Red Cross said 14 adults and five children across seven households had registered with the organization for emergency assistance, which includes temporary lodging.
On Thursday, Ethan Clark and his roommate, DeAndre Finley, left their third-floor apartment on Flatbush Avenue three buildings down from the collapse, holding umbrellas over their heads and carrying several bags of clothes. They were traveling to Harlem to stay with some friends. “If it becomes an extended thing, I don’t know what we’ll do,” Finley said.
The eight people killed when a building in Brooklyn collapsed into a construction site on Wednesday were a cross-section of the bustling, fast-growing Flatbush neighborhood.
They included elementary-school-age cousins, construction workers from Ecuador and Guatemala, and a DoorDash deliveryman and an Amazon worker from Guinea in West Africa, according to an internal police report and the families and friends of the victims.
Six died at the building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue and the construction site next door, where workers were excavating when the building crashed down Wednesday afternoon. Two others were pulled from the wreckage alive but died at hospitals, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a news conference on Thursday.
By midafternoon Thursday, firefighters had halted rescue operations after determining there was no one left in the rubble.
“This has been a devastating evening and morning for our city,” the mayor said earlier.
Another 18 people, including some firefighters, had been injured, Mr. Mamdani said. Officials have not determined what caused the collapse.
Here’s what we know about the victims:
Nicole Daniela Sabala Rodriguez, 9, and Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 11
Nicole and Kevin were cousins, and their family was from Colombia, the Colombian Consulate said. Nicole’s mother, Estefania Rodriguez, was injured in the collapse and was in stable condition at a hospital on Friday, the consulate said.
Juan Daniel Sabala Guzman, 31
Mr. Sabala was the father of Nicole, the 9-year-old who died, the Colombian Consulate said.
Edgar Santiago Sapón Gutierrez, 26
Edgar Santiago Sapón Gutierrez, a 26-year-old construction worker, was working at the site when the building collapsed.
Relatives spent the entire night looking for him, said Marisela Vásquez, 35, whose niece is married to Mr. Sapón.
“We went to the morgue and didn’t find him,” Ms. Vásquez said in Spanish. They returned to the scene of the collapsed building at about 5 or 6 a.m. and saw emergency workers pulling bodies out of the rubble.
“Unfortunately, they told us that he had died,” she said.
Mr. Sapón migrated from Guatemala three years ago, Eliseo Vásquez Talé, his uncle, said. He lived in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, with his 6-year-old son and his wife. She arrived at the scene Wednesday evening after hearing of the collapse, hoping to find him.
“We came to this country to find a better life,” Mr. Vásquez Talé said. “Unfortunately, our government is corrupt.”
On Thursday morning, Mr. Sapón’s family members returned to the morgue, trying to see if they could identify his body. Nobody wants to believe he is dead, Ms. Vásquez said.
“We want to make sure it’s him,” she said.
Mamadou Bhoye Barry, 23, and Mamadou Bhoye N’Diaye, 31
Mamadou Bhoye Barry, 23, and Mamadou Bhoye N’Diaye, 31, were cousins and roommates from Guinea whose bodies were pulled from the rubble an hour apart early on Thursday morning.
“These two young men came to the United States less than five years ago in pursuit of better opportunities and brighter futures,” Mamadou Saliou Diallo, the president of the Guinean Community of America in New York, said at a news conference on Friday. “Sadly, their life has been cut short by this devastating tragedy.”
Mr. Barry, a food delivery worker, and Mr. N’Diaye, who worked at an Amazon warehouse in Brooklyn, were both getting ready to go to work on Wednesday evening, their cousin, Abubakar Diallo, 47, said. But they never made it.
Mamadou Mouctar Balde, who lived with the two men along with his pregnant wife, said that he had left the apartment about five minutes before the building collapsed. Mr. Balde said he had told his wife, Fatoumatabinta Bah, that he was going to buy some things.
As he was leaving, Mr. Barry was cooking. When Mr. Balde opened the front door, a delivery man arrived with a package for Mr. N’Diaye, who was lying down. Mr. Balde called out to him.
“He got up,” Mr. Balde said in French. “I see him today in my heart getting dressed to go get his package.” He broke down as he tried to continue speaking and then wiped tears from his face.
Ms. Bah was severely injured, but she survived along with her unborn child, Mamadou Saliou Diallo said at the news conference.
José Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26
José Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26, a construction worker at the site of the collapse, had recently found work after a period of unemployment.
While he was looking for work in September, he would pick up his 4-year-old son at a pre-K near his family’s home in Bushwick, Brooklyn, said Alexandra Simonian, the son’s teacher.
“When the dad would drop him off, he didn’t want to leave the dad, ever,” Ms. Simonian said. “They were very attached, a very sweet kind of family.”
Mr. Caguana, an immigrant from Ecuador who came to New York at least four years ago, was supporting a growing family: His wife is expecting a child this month, Ms. Simonian said.
On Thursday, Ms. Simonian said, Mr. Caguana’s wife, Nataly, and son came early to school.
“She was asking if it’s OK if he doesn’t come to school this week, because of the dad passing away,” Ms. Simonian said. “She was crying, and we were all hugging her.”
Mr. Caguana was also an avid soccer player. An official from his soccer club in New York, Club Deportivo La Bahía, posted on Facebook, “I will always remember you as a unique player, with that special magic in your feet.”
On Friday, there was a memorial for Mr. Caguana at his apartment in Bushwick. On a table draped with three soccer jerseys, there was a photo of Mr. Caguana crouching with a trophy and medals. Beside it were bouquets of flowers.
Gabriel Siguencia, 22
Gabriel Siguencia could have left work at the construction site early on Wednesday, but he stayed to put in a few extra hours to make money to send back to his 4-year-old son and his wife in Ecuador, his family said.
Mr. Siguencia, who came to New York in March 2025 and lived in the Parkchester section of the Bronx, had just started work as a carpenter on the site a few weeks ago, his stepsister Kayla Chimborazo said, and was very excited that he had finally found a career that would provide for his family.
She said that on Wednesday after the collapse, the family got a call from a co-worker telling them that Mr. Siguencia had stayed late at work.
A family friend, Javier Ortega, said in Spanish, “He came here looking for a better life, a means to live, like so many migrants do.”
Mr. Siguencia’s mother, Leanor Yupa, arrived at the collapse site on Wednesday night in search of news about her son. She and her husband, draped in a blanket, waited all night on the sidewalk, watching emergency workers haul debris out of the site.
On Thursday afternoon, Ms. Yupa and family members sheltered from the pouring rain beneath an overhang. When she finally heard her son had died, Ms. Yupa dropped to her knees and screamed.
Kaja Andric, Miles G. Cohen, Maria Cramer, Luis Ferré-Sadurní, Ana Ley, Chelsia Rose Marcius, Wesley Parnell, Nate Schweber and Rachel Sherman contributed reporting. Jay Root contributed translation. Kitty Bennett contributed research.
An earlier version of this article misspelled the first name of a relative of one of the victims. She is Kayla Chimborazo, not Kyla.
We acknowledge mistakes in our reporting with corrections. If you spot an error, please let us know at corrections@nytimes.com.Learn more.
An hour and a half after a building collapsed into a construction site in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn on Wednesday, a man walked through a crowd of onlookers and arrived at a strip of yellow police tape. He tried to push his way into the scene, but emergency workers blocked his path. It was unsafe to enter, they said.
The man, who did not give his name, paused. His wife was trapped inside, he said. And she was six months pregnant.
He walked across Flatbush Avenue, where he stood on the sidewalk surrounded by police officers, journalists and Jumaane Williams, the city’s public advocate. After nearly an hour of waiting, a journalist relayed the news at 6:30 p.m.: The man’s wife had been found, alive.
The man broke down crying and was embraced by Mr. Williams.
“She is still alive,” the man said in an impromptu news conference near the scene. “I am very happy.”
More than a dozen firefighters worked to lift the woman, who was strapped to an orange stretcher, out of the pit. She was carried to the open doors of an ambulance. Her husband stood by her stretcher for a few minutes before she was loaded into the back. The man climbed into the cab of the ambulance, which took them to a hospital.
The woman is in stable condition, said Farah Louis, the councilwoman who represents the neighborhood. The rescued woman is from Guinea, and she lived in the building with other residents who were immigrants, including from West Africa, Ms. Louis said.
“These folks are our neighbors,” Ms. Louis said. “They’re our friends. That’s why the community is so heartbroken.”
The collapse has killed at least eight people and injured at least 17. In addition to the pregnant woman, other people were removed from the rubble in stretchers, including a small child.
A 26-year-old construction worker, Edgar Santiago Sapón Gutierrez, has been identified as a victim of the collapse.
Relatives had spent the entire night looking for him, said Marisela Vasquez, 35, whose niece is married to Gutierrez. “We went to the morgue and didn’t find him,” Vasquez said. They returned to the collapse site early in the morning and saw emergency workers pulling bodies out of the rubble. “Unfortunately, they told us that he had died,” she said. Gutierrez has a 6-year-old son.
By noon, officials had confirmed that Gutiérrez was among those killed, according to an internal police report.
The Buildings Department said that the license of the special inspector overseeing foundation work at the construction site adjacent to the collapsed building was active, and that city records that indicated that the license had expired was based on information on the old portal. It remains unclear if the inspector had been on site recently.
A complaint filed with the Department of Buildings on Wednesday night, after the building collapse, raised concerns about the excavation work at the adjacent development site, at 2625 Bedford Avenue. The anonymous complainant said the “subcontractor may have excavated too much of the area along the neighboring foundation” on a site with sandy soil and high groundwater.
Complaints are sometimes filed with the city after a major building failure, but it is unclear who submitted the report. The Buildings Department said it was investigating the report, and noted that the complaint was filed “by a member of the public” at 9 p.m., five hours after the collapse.
The site of the collapsed building in Flatbush, Brooklyn, was somber on Thursday as emergency workers removed debris and rubble. The wall of a neighboring building appeared to have come down in the collapse. A bedroom with a pink motif was visible on the second floor. On the first floor, clothes were hanging in a closet.
Mamdani said that he was “incredibly troubled” by reports that construction continued at the site even though an inspection report showed there were cracks in the north facade of the collapsed building. He stressed that the city would conduct a full investigation of the situation and hold anyone responsible “fully accountable.”

articles.title: What Happened to 3Com?
articles.body:
3Com was a high flying maker of network cards and other network equipment. And then they disappeared with a whimper on November 11, 2009. What happened to 3Com?
3Com at the dotcom boom
Around the time of the dotcom boom, 3Com was a 5.8 billion dollar company. They were founded in 1979 by Bob Metcalfe, the co-inventor of Ethernet. And for the next two decades, they were the go-to brand for network cards. While the 3C501 network card is notoriously bad, their other cards from the 1980s and 1990s are very well regarded, and always were.
They cost more, but had good driver support, the hardware worked reliably, and they were a known quantity. And 3Com made them in the United States, which was becoming unusual even in the 1990s.
I once worked in a shop that didn’t allow network equipment unless it was one of three brands. 3Com was one of them, along with Cisco and Intel. If you plugged a no name NE2000 clone card into the network and had problems, the IT department would replace the card and bill your department. There was a saying in the 1980s that no one got fired for buying IBM. When it came to networking, one could say the same for 3Com, during their prime.
And they were huge. In 1995, 3Com bought the naming rights to Candlestick Park, the legendary baseball/football stadium in San Francisco. It held those rights until 2002.
How 3Com’s long decline happened
But after the dotcom bust, 3Com faded away. What happened to 3Com, ultimately, was a series of bad decisions that led to a loss of profitability. Some of them may have made sense at the time. But not all of them.
The first thing that happened was 3Com walked away from its enterprise networking equipment business. Admittedly Cisco was hard to compete with. But 3Com was the only brand succeeding at doing it. The logic behind the move always puzzled analysts, because it didn’t save any money. Revenue dropped, and 3Com angered its customers and dealers. It’s likely many started buying Intel cards afterward, since they had to change vendors anyway.
Many corporations like to buy multiple things from a single supplier. This was one reason IBM stayed in the PC business for several years into the 21st century even though they were losing money on it. The computers weren’t profitable, but they made it easier to sell services, and the services were profitable. There is always the fear that two vendors will point fingers at each other, saying the network problem was caused by the hub and the network card being mismatched brands. Interoperability was the whole idea behind Ethernet, but not everyone understood that. One could commend 3Com for not wanting to exploit that misunderstanding. But it came at a financial cost.
It also didn’t help that the company branched into other businesses outside its core. The purchase of US Robotics was a key example. US Robotics made modems and Palm Pilots. For a short time, that was big business. But 3Com paid a premium price for products with a limited shelf life left in them.
Nothing good happened to 3Com after that. It took 3 years for Cisco to go from being 90% the size of 3Com to double the size of 3Com. The profitability of selling network adapters dropped. And by the time 3Com realized they needed to get back into network equipment, it was an expensive proposition. From 2000 to 2005, the company didn’t turn a profit.
Why 3Com failed
Ultimately, 3Com failed because it was too dependent on network cards. Network cards accounted for about half their revenue during their bust years. And their cards were expensive. Intel undercut their price to try to gain market share, and they succeeded.
And then they did exactly the wrong thing. It was the late ’90s, and they bought their way into the modem business. The dial-up modem business. At that point in time, everyone knew broadband was the future, they just didn’t know exactly when it was going to arrive. Yet 3Com had no plan to get into that business. It was like betting on AOL even though they were in the position to know the future belonged to AT&T.
Making matters worse, minimum viable product-style modems undercut US Robotics modems, just like the network card business. Not that Intel cards were a minimum viable product. But pretty much any ’90s network card not made by Intel or 3Com was.
3Com sought partnerships, most notably a partnership with Chinese networking giant Huawei. There were even rumors of Huawei buying 3com, though that deal never went through. And 3Com started making product overseas as a cost reducing measure. But ultimately, nothing could make up for all that lost time and all those bad decisions.
Who bought 3com
So what happened to 3Com? 3Com didn’t go out of business and they didn’t sell out to Huawei. They got Compaqed. Hewlett-Packard bought them out, which seems to be where every great ’90s technology company went to die. Hewlett-Packard paid 2.7 billion dollars in late 2009 for 3Com’s assets.
HP still sells network equipment like switches, routers, and access points. But they’re not as big of a name in networking as 3Com had been. And the 3Com pedigree isn’t the selling point. If they put a brand on it other than HP, it’s the newer Aruba brand, not 3Com. The selling point is the price being lower than Cisco. This makes them attractive to executives or purchasing agents looking to cut costs, consolidate vendors, or both. HP will usually beat Cisco’s price. And if the IT department is under pressure to reduce the number of vendors it buys from, HP sells more things than Cisco. So HP gets in the door for one of those reasons, and when their network equipment turns out to be no worse than Cisco equipment, they stay with it. At least until Dell comes around offering discounts.
But the network cards are long gone. When you buy an HP branded network card today, guess what it is? It’s an Intel card with HP’s logo engraved on it. Unless HP is trying to control costs, in which case it just has a sticker.
3Com today
Vintage 3Com network cards are very popular with retro computing enthusiasts. It had top-tier name recognition in the 80s and 90s. All but their very earliest cards generally have good driver support, work well, and are easier to configure than most of the cheaper competitors.
My favorite retro network card is a very specific Intel card, but if you need a card for anything from the 286 to the Pentium II era, you can do far worse than a 3com 3c509 ISA card or 3c905 PCI card. It’s absolutely period correct and absolutely something a knowledgeable professional would have used at the time. I have better luck with the ISA cards under DOS than the PCI cards, so if I want to run DOS and do any networking, I use a 3c509 ISA card in the system. But for Windows 95 and newer, the 3c905 PCI card works really well and is very cheap and common.
David Farquhar is a computer security professional, entrepreneur, and author. He has written professionally about computers since 1991, so he was writing about retro computers when they were still new. He has been working in IT professionally since 1994 and has specialized in vulnerability management since 2013. He holds Security+ and CISSP certifications. Today he blogs five times a week, mostly about retro computers and retro gaming covering the time period from 1975 to 2000.

articles.title: Global Microsoft Outage
articles.body:
Our live coverage has ended
Read more about the Microsoft outage here or scroll through the posts below to learn more.
Updates
(29)
Where things stand with the disruptive Microsoft service outage
• Coming back online: Microsoft said it has addressed the underlying issue of a massive outage that affected millions around the world as it continues to restore service. The software giant apologized for disruptions, saying the outage was caused by a technical issue and not a cybersecurity breach.
• Economic ramifications: The cost of lost productivity from the outage could approach at least $7 billion, according to a think-tank estimate.
• What’s been impacted: The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life. AI companies said they were facing issues as well. Banks, governments, health services, railways and courts all reported disruptions across Microsoft products.
• Global disruption: Outage reports “reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour,” according to Downdetector. While some workers scrambled to find workarounds, others expressed relief in a respite from the work grind.
US city governments say services are returning after outage
US cities are beginning to report Microsoft services returning after a widespread outage that began yesterday hit governments across the country and world.
Jacksonville, Florida, said that it was “seeing some services restored this morning and remain cautiously optimistic they will continue making progress.”
Austin and Dallas also reported progress on their email services being restored. The sheriff’s office in Arapahoe County, Colorado, which had previously reported the outage affecting online bond payments, said the issue was resolved.
Microsoft said this morning that the “underlying issue” that caused the massive outage had been addressed and that it was seeing recovery across its services.
The police department of Greensboro, North Carolina, also saw its services being restored. “While it’s not the outcome we wanted, we would like to let you know that our email is working again,” the department jested.
Microsoft services returning to normal after hours of disruption. Catch up on the latest
After hours of disruption affecting millions of users worldwide, Outlook and other Microsoft services are finally returning to normal.
Microsoft has apologized for the outage, which could end up costing billions in lost productivity.
The company reported “encouraging recovery progress” saying that queues of emails waiting to be delivered are “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.”
Here’s what to know:
What was disrupted? Any of the applications involving email or Microsoft’s Exchange Online Services were affected, the company said. That left users likely unable to access or send new emails, use Microsoft’s AI tool Copilot, or join pre-scheduled Teams meetings already in the calendar. Other services — like those that share documents, pool a company’s data or protect emails — might also have been affected.
What’s the impact? The outage left millions without the work tools they use every day and could cost $7 billion in lost productivity, according to an estimate by a Michigan think tank. Patrick Anderson, Anderson Economic Group’s president, said that perhaps as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million users on Friday have actually seen their operations disrupted in a way that caused an economic loss. And he said the cost will likely increase beyond this initial estimate.
City governments across the US reported disruption, encouraging residents to call local offices if necessary. Some Brits experienced delays in getting their drug prescriptions and several UK police forces told the public to report crimes or issues by telephone rather than through their websites.
Meanwhile, bank workers in Hong Kong had their work disrupted, government employees in Japan resorted to creating physical copies of documents and courts in the Philippines were hindered by the outage. Some railway networks experienced disruption to their customer email services and routing schedules while Australian schools, courts and government services reported disruption.
What caused this? Microsoft said the outage was caused by a “technical issue” rather than any cybersecurity breach. “The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change,” the company said.
CNN’s Gage Goulding, Anna Cooban, August Phillips, Hanna Ziady, Karina Tsui, Helen Regan, Kathleen Magramo and Chris Isidore contributed reporting
Microsoft apologizes, says underlying cause of outage has been addressed
Microsoft has addressed the “underlying issue” that caused a massive outage affecting millions across the world, the tech company said, adding that it was “seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.”
Microsoft offered some explanation of what caused the outage that began yesterday, confirming it was a “technical issue” and not a cybersecurity or AI-related concern.
“The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change,” Microsoft said.
The software giant said it would release a “full post-incident report” after a review.
Cost of Microsoft outage could top $7 billion, according to estimate
The cost of lost productivity from the Microsoft outage could approach $7 billion, according to an estimate by a Michigan think tank on Friday.
Anderson Economic Group, which is known for cautious estimates on the costs of economic disruptions, including labor strikes and tariffs, said that many of the reported 430 million Microsoft users who have been affected likely only are dealing with annoyances, rather than true lost productivity.
But Patrick Anderson, the firm’s president, said that perhaps as many as 26 million users on Thursday and 51 million users on Friday have actually seen their operations disrupted in a way that caused an economic loss. And he said the cost will likely increase beyond this initial estimate.
“This is a starting point, with all the limitations on what we know. We don’t know complete scale,” he told CNN on Friday.
Some companies might be able to be compensated by cybersecurity insurance policies for the costs associated with the outage – but that would only shift the cost from the Microsoft users to their insurers.
In addition, Anderson estimated that Microsoft could conceivably need to refund customers about $800 million a day in subscription fees for services they pay for under contracts but could not access. While not all customers will seek refunds, those who do so are likely to push the total cost of the outage above $7 billion, Anderson said.
The outage, which began around noon ET on Thursday, left workers unable to access Outlook email, Teams meeting tools and other staples of modern office life, as well as the company’s Copilot AI chatbot.
Emails are "approaching normal levels” after outage, Microsoft says
Outlook is returning to normal after hours of disruption, as queues of email waiting to be delivered are “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels,” Microsoft said.
The company is continuing to observe “improvements in service availability,” it said in a statement this morning. “Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues,” it added.
Microsoft seeing "broader improvements" in North America
Microsoft just said it is seeing “encouraging recovery progress” at the same time as some social media users and CNN journalists report receiving emails in their inboxes again.
In a statement on X, the company reported “email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure,” but warned some users may still “experience intermittent issues.”
While some social media users reported getting emails again, others said they were still unable to access them.
In an additional update issued later, Microsoft outlined the uneven pace of recovery in different regions. The company indicated that North America was recovering faster than Europe and Asia.
It reported “broader improvements in North America, sustained improvements across much of Europe, and encouraging recovery signals in Asia Pacific.”
UK police forces urge public to report crimes via telephone, not online
Several UK police forces told the public Friday to report crimes or issues by telephone rather than through their websites amid the Microsoft outage.
Police forces in Merseyside, Greater Manchester and Bedfordshire informed visitors to their websites that online submission forms were disrupted.
East Hertfordshire Police said in a statement posted to X that “some online form submissions on our website may be affected” because of the outage.
In another Friday post on X, Dorset Police said it was “unable to receive online form submissions.”
All police forces urged the public to call 101 if their issue is “time-critical but not an emergency.” (The UK emergency number is 999).
Microsoft says services are being "gradually restored"
Microsoft says it is making “additional progress toward recovery” and that traffic is “being gradually restored” as its engineers scramble to fix the worldwide outage that has left millions without the work tools they use every day.
In a statement, Microsoft said it is “seeing improvements in key scenarios, including mailbox access and delayed email processing, though some intermittent issues may continue.”
What to know as you're waking up in the US without email
Outlook is still down, as Microsoft’s rolling outage – now extending into a second day – continues to affect services for millions of people around the world.
The outage, which is also affecting Teams and Copilot, is disrupting government and business operations in the United States and elsewhere, with at least one company postponing a quarterly earnings call.
Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna said in the early hours of Friday that there is currently no indication that the outage is the result “of malicious or cyber activity.”
Here’s what to know:
Email down: Outlook remains down and users are also having trouble accessing their Exchange Online mailboxes.
In an update at around 4:15 a.m. ET Friday, Microsoft said it would extend its “email timeout window” to 48 hours “to help protect delayed messages while service recovery continues.”
The email timeout window is the maximum amount of time that a mail server or email client such as Outlook will spend waiting to receive an email before returning an error.
AI companies affected: OpenAI said it was facing issues with Microsoft connectors, with some tools, including ChatGPT, not working “as expected.” Meanwhile, thousands of Claude AI users reported issues Friday morning, according to Downdetector. Claude creator Anthropic said shortly after 6 a.m. ET that a fix had been deployed and it was “monitoring for recovery.”
US lawmakers: The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft, according to Reuters. Some congressional staffers expressed frustration on X. “Shall we start conducting all official business via DM?” said Sharon Eliza Nichols, communications director for Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton.
US cities: City governments across the United States have reported email disruptions and have encouraged residents to call local offices and agencies if necessary.
- Several police and sheriff departments said the outage was affecting their email and communication platforms, including Colorado’s Arapahoe Sheriff’s Office, which said the outage had delayed the processing of prisoners’ bail payments.
- The outages are affecting email services in Miami Beach, Austin, and Jacksonville, though officials assured residents that emergency services were still active.
- In California, officials from Pasadena, Fremont, Burbank, and Santa Barbara also issued statements warning of downed email use.
- Baltimore County officials said on X that government staff could not send or receive emails and urged residents to contact relevant departments by phone.
Earnings call delayed: Workhorse Group, a Detroit-based electric vehicle manufacturer, pushed its third quarter earnings call to Monday, citing “business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outages.”
CNN’s Gage Goulding contributed reporting.
What is affected by the outage?
Some office workers rely on Microsoft’s suite of applications for practically everything – emails, meetings, AI, creating spreadsheets, and writing and sharing documents. Any of those functions which involve email or Microsoft’s Exchange Online services are impacted, the company said.
Outlook: Email is the main thing impacted by the outage, leaving users likely unable to access or send any new emails.
Copilot: Users may also be unable to load chats with or receive responses from Microsoft’s AI tool. Copilot also cannot access the data it normally draws from, like emails, files and calendars.

articles.title: Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
articles.body:
Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom — and one of the tech industry’s biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories, drained power grids from inside massive data centers, and set the stage for a looming e-waste problem.
Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
Nvidia’s environmental footprint extends way beyond its own offices.
Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia clashed with environmental groups seeking to hold the company accountable for its so-called “hidden” emissions. Huang has talked up the idea of using AI to fight climate change while his company’s supply chain emissions ballooned. Nvidia’s investments, meanwhile, have supported the buildout of data centers that have sparked intense backlash for both their local and global impact. Now, after the CEO’s shocking resignation amid a sprawling sex-and-espionage scandal, advocates are urging Nvidia to turn the page.
He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
“Jensen Huang has failed to put climate responsibility at the heart of the company’s growth strategy, to slow down the unchecked expansion of data centres or to prevent its chips from being deployed in unethical applications like automated warfare,” Avex Li, Greenpeace East Asia’s project lead for AI supply chain campaign, said in a press release Thursday. The organization is now pushing interim CEO Colette Kress to commit Nvidia to decarbonizing by investing in renewable energy, as well as ensuring its technology is used in a way that “respects human rights.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge.
Huang has projected optimism about how AI can boost the adoption of renewable energy, even as the planet-heating emissions of tech companies — including his own — have grown in the generative AI era. “If you want to turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable, lean into A.I. It is the best opportunity we have to get there,” Huang said in a September episode of The Ezra Klein Show, arguing that electricity demand for AI is leading companies to buy more sustainable energy.
In the same interview, however, he admitted data centers will rely on more fossil fuels in the near term, and that building up the infrastructure for AI will likely result in “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
Nvidia’s supply-chain emissions have grown 725 percent since 2020, according to an analysis of the company’s public disclosures by research analyst Ketan Joshi and several environmental organizations, including Greenpeace and Climate Action Against Disinformation, published in September. It’s an increase of about 9.4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10.7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report.
Joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category Nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Those emissions could have reached 21 million metric tons in 2025, according to the report, based on estimated chip power consumption. That level of pollution puts Nvidia on par with Russia’s state-owned coal company, according to Joshi.
Those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of Nvidia’s climate impact. The carbon footprint of facilities Nvidia actually owns and operates looks much smaller in comparison because Nvidia designs chips that other companies like TSMC then manufacture. Greenhouse gas emissions coming directly from Nvidia-operated facilities and vehicles only reached 9,822 metric tons in fiscal year 2026, the company’s sustainability report shows. And in 2025, the company reached a goal of matching 100 percent of its facilities’ electricity use with clean energy purchases.
Greenpeace wants Nvidia to extend that goal to its entire manufacturing supply chain. When Greenpeace activists disrupted Huang’s speech at Nvidia GTC in Berlin last month, he responded onstage by saying, “I’ll talk to you guys later … All important issues, but let me get through my keynote.” In the Thursday press release, Greenpeace says Nvidia has yet to meet with Greenpeace despite the organization’s attempts to “seek dialogue” with the company over the past two years.
“One of Huang’s defining legacies is inflating a speculative AI bubble, pouring billions of dollars into infrastructure with little regard for the real-world consequences inflicted on local communities and the climate,” Katrin Wu, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in an email to The Verge. “Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
“Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
Beyond Nvidia’s day-to-day operations, Huang threw his weight around as the CEO of one of the world’s most valuable companies — chumming it up with President Donald Trump and lobbying for the US to allow sales of its powerful chips to China. The company’s influence on the global economy extended beyond chips as it invested in data centers stocking its GPUs.
And with electricity supply often the thorniest bottleneck to building more and bigger data centers, Nvidia’s long tendrils reached into the energy sector as well. NVentures, the company’s venture capital arm, has funded battery recycling company Redwood Materials and startups developing AI tools to optimize power grids and make data centers more responsive to fluctuations in energy demand.
Nvidia joined one of those startups, Emerald AI, along with Google to cofound the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) in September. The alliance advocates for strategies that tech companies promote as ways to keep data centers from overwhelming power grids or raising utility bills for other customers, including generating power on-site and making “flexible” facilities that can pause operations during times of peak energy demand. Notably, some environmental groups argue that those measures might just help data centers come online faster without fully insulating households from the impact that rising electricity demand has on their air quality or utility bills.
Whether Nvidia’s environmental footprint shrinks or expands from here will depend on whoever steps in to fill Huang’s shoes. Over the years, Greenpeace and other environmental groups have pointed out that despite having an outsize impact on the environment, Nvidia doesn’t necessarily come under the same public scrutiny as more consumer-facing brands like Apple or Google. Huang’s exploits have thrust the company into a new kind of spotlight, however, just as data centers increasingly face backlash from nearby communities. Nvidia won’t be able to hide from the glare.

/*
 * This is an implementation of wcwidth() (defined in
 * IEEE Std 1002.1-2001) for Unicode.
 *
 * http://www.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/007904975/functions/wcwidth.html
 *
 * In fixed-width output devices, Latin characters all occupy a single
 * "cell" position of equal width, whereas ideographic CJK characters
 * occupy two such cells. Interoperability between terminal-line
 * applications and (teletype-style) character terminals using the
 * UTF-8 encoding requires agreement on which character should advance
 * the cursor by how many cell positions. No established formal
 * standards exist at present on which Unicode character shall occupy
 * how many cell positions on character terminals. These routines are
 * a first attempt of defining such behavior based on simple rules
 * applied to data provided by the Unicode Consortium.
 *
 * For some graphical characters, the Unicode standard explicitly
 * defines a character-cell width via the definition of the East Asian
 * FullWidth (F), Wide (W), Half-width (H), and Narrow (Na) classes.
 * In all these cases, there is no ambiguity about which width a
 * terminal shall use. For characters in the East Asian Ambiguous (A)
 * class, the width choice depends purely on a preference of backward
 * compatibility with either historic CJK or Western practice.
 * Choosing single-width for these characters is easy to justify as
 * the appropriate long-term solution, as the CJK practice of
 * displaying these characters as double-width comes from historic
 * implementation simplicity (8-bit encoded characters were displayed
 * single-width and 16-bit ones double-width, even for Greek,
 * Cyrillic, etc.) and not any typographic considerations.
 *
 * Much less clear is the choice of width for the Not East Asian
 * (Neutral) class. Existing practice does not dictate a width for any
 * of these characters. It would nevertheless make sense
 * typographically to allocate two character cells to characters such
 * as for instance EM SPACE or VOLUME INTEGRAL, which cannot be
 * represented adequately with a single-width glyph. The following
 * routines at present merely assign a single-cell width to all
 * neutral characters, in the interest of simplicity. This is not
 * entirely satisfactory and should be reconsidered before
 * establishing a formal standard in this area. At the moment, the
 * decision which Not East Asian (Neutral) characters should be
 * represented by double-width glyphs cannot yet be answered by
 * applying a simple rule from the Unicode database content. Setting
 * up a proper standard for the behavior of UTF-8 character terminals
 * will require a careful analysis not only of each Unicode character,
 * but also of each presentation form, something the author of these
 * routines has avoided to do so far.

版权与许可声明
APP: GPLv3 with the FM1 SDK linking exception; no warranty. SDK and firmware resources have separate redistribution terms in THIRD_PARTY.md. Source: https://open.m-vave.com/releases/V14/6324230590b8e332bc544128abd7b919a2efd5982db60ea9a11663d4ea820344/FM1-Open-V14-Development-Kit-copy-update.zip
FM-1 V15 recovery firmware: https://www.m-vave.com/download (PC Firmware / FM-1 V15). Distributed by M-VAVE under Apache-2.0. Retain applicable licenses and notices; components with separate licenses retain their terms. See THIRD_PARTY.md.
===== THIRD_PARTY.md =====
# Third-party notices
Project-owned public APP sources: [GPLv3 with the FM1 SDK linking exception](LICENSE.md). Component licenses also apply to firmware and web builds that include those components.
| Component | Source / license |
| --- | --- |
| 303 | [Open303](https://github.com/RobinSchmidt/Open303/tree/313bf0d9ade7c1dcb6b3a74f5ea1780a29d70074), MIT; C adaptation with FM1 drive and MIDI handling. |
| 808 / Pluck | [DaisySP](https://github.com/daisyaudio/DaisySP/tree/2c72eaf9eac5fc0dca1919d65d606da907832618), MIT; selected Plaits drum and String models with FM1 voices and controls. |
| SVF | [stmlib](https://github.com/pichenettes/stmlib/tree/d18def816c51d1da0c108236928b2bbd25c17481), MIT; fixed-rate filter adaptation. |
| FM model | [MSFA](https://github.com/google/music-synthesizer-for-android/tree/f67d41d313b7dc85f6fb99e79e515cc9d208cfff) / [Dexed msfa](https://github.com/asb2m10/dexed/tree/eebb748b70c5a1338afa3945e8b1ea783c9c02fe/source/msfa), Apache-2.0; C adaptation of algorithms, envelopes, LFO and note scaling, with FM1 arithmetic and controls. |
| PSG | [emu2149](https://github.com/digital-sound-antiques/emu2149/tree/441f3dc295a9b82db16921461f0678b483db8304), MIT; memory/table adaptation and ultrasonic output fix. |
| SEA codec | [SEA](https://github.com/Daninet/sea-codec), MIT; fixed-format encoder, decoder and tables. |
| Packager | [jl-misctools](https://github.com/kagaimiq/jl-misctools/tree/0a5b12db0ef38f3042acffbe2452730a37fd2405), MIT; format/codec adaptation with FM1 validation and layout. |
| Native C runtime | `sdk/lib/libc.a`, Newlib-derived routines; native runtime notices below. |
| Native compiler runtime | `sdk/lib/libcompiler_rt.a`; identified compiler-rt routines, legacy MIT / University of Illinois-NCSA notices below.  |
| micro-ecc | Identified routines in `sdk/lib/libfm1_engine.a`; BSD-2-Clause notice below. |
| JieLi SDK material | Identified AC79 SDK material retains its upstream terms; see SDK notices below. |
| APP / open web engine tuning | Incorporates contributions by [Vikram Rojo (PR #2)](https://github.com/m-vave/fm1_open/pull/2), with FM1 integration changes (2026-10-17). Original file licenses and notices are retained. |
| Configuration resource | `sdk/tools/pack/cfg_tool.bin`, identical to the file in the identified official JieLi Apache-2.0 SDK distribution; see below. |
| Boot/update resources and recovery firmware | `sdk/tools/pack/uboot.boot`, `ota.bin`, `boot-config.bin`, and `sdk/firmware/FM-1_015.fwsc`, Apache-2.0; see the resource terms below. |
| Original 128-voice DX7 bank | `app/fm_factory.inc`: extracted without parameter or ordering changes from the bundled M-VAVE V15 recovery image (Apache-2.0), losslessly encoded for Flash in 2026. Reproduce with `node tools/Generate-Factory-DX7.mjs`; the tool pins the source package and decoded VMEM SHA-256 hashes. Demo project recipes remain separate. |

libc/string/wcwidth.c
/*
 * This is an implementation of wcwidth() (defined in
 * IEEE Std 1002.1-2001) for Unicode.
 *
 * http://www.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/007904975/functions/wcwidth.html
 *
 * In fixed-width output devices, Latin characters all occupy a single
 * "cell" position of equal width, whereas ideographic CJK characters
 * occupy two such cells. Interoperability between terminal-line
 * applications and (teletype-style) character terminals using the
 * UTF-8 encoding requires agreement on which character should advance
 * the cursor by how many cell positions. No established formal
 * standards exist at present on which Unicode character shall occupy
 * how many cell positions on character terminals. These routines are
 * a first attempt of defining such behavior based on simple rules
 * applied to data provided by the Unicode Consortium.
 *
 * For some graphical characters, the Unicode standard explicitly
 * defines a character-cell width via the definition of the East Asian
 * FullWidth (F), Wide (W), Half-width (H), and Narrow (Na) classes.
 * In all these cases, there is no ambiguity about which width a
 * terminal shall use. For characters in the East Asian Ambiguous (A)
 * class, the width choice depends purely on a preference of backward
 * compatibility with either historic CJK or Western practice.
 * Choosing single-width for these characters is easy to justify as
 * the appropriate long-term solution, as the CJK practice of
 * displaying these characters as double-width comes from historic
 * implementation simplicity (8-bit encoded characters were displayed
 * single-width and 16-bit ones double-width, even for Greek,
 * Cyrillic, etc.) and not any typographic considerations.
 *
 * Much less clear is the choice of width for the Not East Asian
 * (Neutral) class. Existing practice does not dictate a width for any
 * of these characters. It would nevertheless make sense
 * typographically to allocate two character cells to characters such
 * as for instance EM SPACE or VOLUME INTEGRAL, which cannot be
 * represented adequately with a single-width glyph. The following
 * routines at present merely assign a single-cell width to all
 * neutral characters, in the interest of simplicity. This is not
 * entirely satisfactory and should be reconsidered before
 * establishing a formal standard in this area. At the moment, the
 * decision which Not East Asian (Neutral) characters should be
 * represented by double-width glyphs cannot yet be answered by
 * applying a simple rule from the Unicode database content. Setting
 * up a proper standard for the behavior of UTF-8 character terminals
 * will require a careful analysis not only of each Unicode character,
 * but also of each presentation form, something the author of these
 * routines has avoided to do so far.
 *
 * http://www.unicode.org/unicode/reports/tr11/
 *
 * Markus Kuhn -- 2007-05-26 (Unicode 5.0)
 *
 * Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software
 * for any purpose and without fee is hereby granted. The author
 * disclaims all warranties with regard to this software.
 *
 * Latest version: http://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~mgk25/ucs/wcwidth.c
 */
